discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in moire materials

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional materials and correlated electrons
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that two graphene sheets twisted to about 1.1 degrees develop nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions should dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and his group realised this with a controlled 'tear-and-stack' fabrication method. Their transport measurements revealed correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in pure carbon, tuned simply by a gate voltage. The experiment is unambiguous, and the work created an entirely new platform: the twist angle is now a design parameter. Moire materials have since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene. This is a rare case where a clean theoretical prediction and ingenious device physics together opened a field that now shapes research on correlated and topological quantum matter worldwide.
